title: Verticillium wilt on Edible African Eggplant

Header: Verticillium wilt on Edible African Eggplant

Prevention: Verticillium wilt is most successful using a multifaceted strategy.
There is no satisfactory control for this disease once plants are infected
Avoid moving soils or debris from areas of known infection
Disinfect all tools between cuts with a 10% solution of household bleach or 70% alcohol.
Long rotation of 4-5 years with other crops other than potatoes, tomatoes, and peppers is recommended
Grafting eggplants on resistant rootstocks reduces severity
Monitoring: Monitor the field and look out for wilting plants
Note that most symptoms are found on the stems and roots
Perform a lengthwise cut of the infected stem.
A dark-brown discoloration will be observed in the vascular tissue
The affected leaves turn yellow and then brown between veins followed by wilting and dropping off.
After the plant is thoroughly invaded, the roots and the base of the stem may decay
As soon as symptoms are observed, follow direct control measures
Direct Control: Fungicides are not effective for control, but if plants exhibit mild symptoms, maintain vigour by following sound cultural practices.
Mulching to help maintain soil moisture and moderate soil temperatures.
Control weeds because the fungus can infect a variety of common weeds such as ragweed, cocklebur, and velvetleaf
Restrictions: Soil-borne disease so chemicals are not recommended.
Wear protective clothing when using pesticides.
Follow product label (dosage, timing of application, pre-harvest interval etc.)
Always consult recent list of registered pesticides in your country
